reading.body:
Profit Finder Pro Software is not a data center and should not be counted in any assessment of AI infrastructure or grid load.

The listing is a customer relationship management and sales-tracking product sold to small businesses in roofing, solar, contracting, and insurance. Its address in the Scottsdale area of Maricopa County, Arizona is currently occupied by a different company, TraVek Inc. Nothing publicly available connects the software business or the address to server infrastructure, colocation space, or dedicated data center equipment. The entry originates as a mistagged OpenStreetMap point marked telecom=data_center.

The pattern matters because capacity counts drive conclusions about power. This site carries no published megawatt figure, and the data states it does not contribute to the 512 MW mapped across Arizona's four facilities with published figures. A mistagged office address inflates the count of facilities without adding a single watt, which distorts any reading of how much compute the grid must support.

What the data does not cover is how many other entries carry the same error. It records that this address sits several miles from the other eight rows in its batch, so no shared building connects them, and that each is an independently mistagged small business scattered across the Phoenix metro. That is a statement about one batch, not a rate for the dataset. The research status is exhausted and specifications are unpublished, so there is nothing further to verify here.
